top.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
top.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . top.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
top.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad. top.title: Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent
top.description: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros ($880 million) for accessing users’ photos without their “specific” consent, the country’s data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”. In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for having misled the state’s residents for more than a decade over use of their data — a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression. Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law. That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal. – Facebook gallery feature – The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing. According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery. The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it. In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” — around 20 million Android users in Italy — and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”. The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”. It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5 billion. top.title: 'Everyone knew': Ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers fires fresh salvo at Pat Cummins over sandpaper scandal
top.description: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the South Africa tour. Sayers, who was part of the touring squad, said he believed every player was aware of what was happening. He also disagreed with Cummins’ statement that there was no team discussion about taking collective responsibility after the incident. “I’m comfortable sitting here … that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” Sayers told SEN radio on Sunday. “I’m not taking sides. I’m neutral in all this, I’m just trying to tell my side of the story and what I believe happened.” The controversy has returned to the spotlight following Khawaja’s autobiography, in which he claimed the entire team knew about the sandpaper plan and suggested Australia had used ball-tampering methods even before the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s allegations as “complete nonsense” during a press conference on Friday. However, Sayers was unhappy with how the Australian captain addressed the issue, particularly his personal comments about Khawaja. “I didn’t like how he [Cummins] did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I don’t think it needed to happen.” Sayers recalls team meeting after scandal Sayers also remembered a lengthy discussion among players after the incident came to light. This contradicts Cummins’ version of events. “We all sat in the change rooms after that day’s play, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, and just talked about what had happened and where to next,” Sayers said. He added that he was relieved the matter was finally being discussed openly after years of players having to remain silent. Warner questions Cricket Australia's investigation Meanwhile, former vice-captain David Warner has again questioned Cricket Australia’s investigation, alleging that important information was withheld from him. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was punished following the scandal. Warner claimed he was never informed that bowlers had been interviewed during the investigation and questioned why the governing body had not shared all the evidence with him before he accepted his punishment. “Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote on Instagram. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements. “That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. Why weren’t we given all the evidence by CA?”

top.title: McIlroy wins record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title
top.description: Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy in action at the DP World Tour Championship golf tournament at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai (Fadel SENNA) Rory McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai title to tie the record of Scotland's Colin Montgomerie after a dramatic final round of the season-ending $10 million DP World Tour Championship on Sunday. The tournament itself was a runaway win for England's Tyrrell Hatton (66) but all eyes were on the fascinating battle between McIlroy and Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, playing a group behind. It all came down to the 18th hole, where McIlroy made a disappointing par to finish on 10-under par, but that was good enough for a solo second place. That took his ranking points to 5,044.86. Chacarra also could not get a birdie on the final hole and closed with a 69 for a tied third place at eight-under alongside Finland's Oliver Lindell (65). The European number one crown was secured with a bogey-free round of five-under par 67, but it all came down to the par-4 16th hole, where he hit a magnificent second shot to a foot for the decisive birdie. McIlroy started with a birdie, but the momentum seemed to have been halted over the next four holes, when he burnt the edge on three but could not get a second birdie. He then picked up three shots over the next four holes, but Chacarra kept him in sight with four birdies in his first eight holes. When McIlroy could not make a birdie on the par-5 14th hole, Chacarra was leading the projected ranking by a mere 0.1 point. Hatton finally finished with seven birdies against a solitary mistake on the third hole on a day when he again dazzled with brilliant short iron and wedge play. The win was worth $3 million and he also climbed to third in the Race to Dubai behind McIlroy and Chacarra, his career best finish. top.description: Liverpool could face rivals in move for €40m French star Liverpool Tracking Robin Risser as RC Lens Set €40m Price for Rising Goalkeeper Liverpool’s recruitment has rarely stood still for long and the latest name to drift into view is Robin Risser, the 21-year-old RC Lens goalkeeper who is beginning to draw the kind of attention that changes careers. According to Caught Offside, Liverpool are among the clubs monitoring the Frenchman, with Manchester United also watching closely as Manchester City push to the front of the queue. There is a familiar rhythm to stories like this. A young goalkeeper emerges in Ligue 1, carries himself with authority, shows composure in possession and suddenly the wealthiest clubs in Europe begin circling. Risser appears to fit that pattern neatly. He is said to have the frame, the calmness and the technical level that modern elite sides crave, especially those that ask their goalkeeper to do far more than stop shots. IMAGO Robin Risser Emerges in Liverpool Transfer Talk At 1.93 metres, Risser has the physical presence clubs covet, but it is the broader package that seems to have stirred interest. His comfort on the ball, command in the air and sharpness in one-on-one situations have all added to his growing reputation in France. For Liverpool, those traits matter. Building from the back remains central to how top sides want to play and succession planning in goal is one of the most delicate tasks in football. RC Lens are reportedly holding firm at €40m, which converts to around £34m, for a player under contract until 2030. Strasbourg would also receive 25 per cent of any fee through a sell-on clause, a detail that may harden Lens’ stance further. Manchester City are believed to be preparing a €30m bid, around £25m, so any deal would likely demand both conviction and speed. RC Lens Price Tag Sets Summer Challenge Liverpool’s interest makes sense in principle. Elite clubs have to think ahead before need becomes urgency. top.description: Chelsea see bid rejected for £25m La Liga star Chelsea Transfer News: Jose Antonio Morante Rejection Shows Betis Winger Has a Clear Plan Chelsea’s recruitment machine keeps scanning the market for young talent, and this time the trail led to Jose Antonio Morante. According to Metro, the Blues tried to make headway for the Real Betis winger, only to find the door closed by the player himself. That matters. Clubs can test the waters with agents and intermediaries all they like, but when a 19-year-old decides he would rather stay put and fight for minutes at his boyhood club, that tells you something about his priorities. Morante is not chasing the biggest badge in the room. He is chasing a football plan that suits him. Photo: IMAGO Jose Antonio Morante Chooses Real Betis Path Morante only broke into the Betis first team earlier this year and has made three senior appearances this season. On the surface, those numbers are modest. The context is more revealing. He is a teenager coming through at a serious club, and Betis clearly see value in him. Over the summer he raised his profile considerably with Spain’s UEFA European Under-19 Championship-winning side. A place in the Team of the Tournament and four goals, enough to finish as joint-top scorer, made him one of the standout names in his age group. Chelsea tracked him there and followed up with an approach during the summer window. The answer was no. By all accounts, Morante wants to establish himself as a first-team regular with Real Betis. It is a sensible call, and one plenty of young players could learn from. Real Betis Contract Underlines Chelsea Setback Betis moved quickly in July, tying Morante down until 2030. The new contract also includes a €30 million, £25m, release clause. That is not a token number. It is protection, leverage and a warning to anyone circling. top.title: Eugenio Chacarra’s immediate reaction after losing out to Rory McIlroy in the Race to Dubai
top.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown on Sunday after he finished in second place at the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy posted a superb final round score of 67 to finish two strokes clear of his main rival for the season-long race, Eugenio Chacarra. The Northern Irishman’s second-place finish at the Earth Course secured his fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title. Rory McIlroy has now tied Colin Montgomerie with eight Race to Dubai crowns. It’s fair to say that the six-time major champion was nowhere near his best this week in Dubai, but he did enough to get the job done in the end. Getting that eighth order of merit title under his belt was so important for McIlroy, and now his attention will turn to breaking the record next year. Chacarra came so close to winning his first season-long race, and he gave a great account of himself throughout 2026. Eugenio Chacarra’s reaction after Rory McIlroy wins the Race to Dubai The race between McIlroy and Chacarra went right down to the wire , and the Spaniard deserves huge credit for pushing the Northern Irishman all the way. After his final round on Sunday, Chacarra was asked to share his feelings after just missing out on the order of merit title. “ Yeah, it was a good fight. I just came up short, “ he admitted. “ That’s the beauty of golf, Obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And he’s played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. “ Yeah, I played good. I fought hard. I knew it was going to be a long day and I tried my best. That’s all I can ask for myself to do and that’s what we did. “ As I said yesterday, it was a bonus, and I would say proud of the fight and proud to have a chance till the end. “ Chacarra then commented on the prospect of playing on the PGA Tour next year. “ Yeah, super excited. But I love the DP World Tour. It’s been so much for me and hopefully I can start good over there and come here as much as possible, “ he said.

top.title: Andres Iniesta heaps praise on Lamine Yamal – “Joy to have him as Barcelona and Spain player”
top.description: Andres Iniesta heaps praise on Lamine Yamal – “Joy to have him as Barcelona and Spain player” Lamine Yamal is no stranger to praises from some of the legends of football, having established himself as arguably football’s biggest and most talented young star since Lionel Messi about two decades ago. Having already won the FIFA World Cup and the European Championship with Spain, Yamal has recently received praise from none other than Andres Iniesta. The Barcelona legend has pointed out how Yamal has continued to better himself at every turn and is now one of the unique players in world football. What Iniesta said about Yamal Yamal is growing in confidence every year. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking to DAZN, Iniesta said Yamal has the potential to become a unique star and praised his hard work. “There’s no doubt that Lamine has incredible talent. It’s in his hands to become a unique player,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Iniesta also feels grateful that Yamal is a Spanish and Barcelona player, rather than being a foreign talent. “I hope he continues to improve every year, keeps working on himself and makes the team better. For me, as a Barcelona fan and as a Spaniard, it’s a privilege and a joy to have Lamine playing for Barcelona and the national team,” he added. Iniesta praises Spain national team Iniesta believes Yamal can achieve bigger things. nigeria.title: Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent
nigeria.description: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros ($880 million) for accessing users’ photos without their “specific” consent, the country’s data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”. In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for having misled the state’s residents for more than a decade over use of their data — a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression. Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law. That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal. – Facebook gallery feature – The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing. According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery. The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it. In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” — around 20 million Android users in Italy — and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”. The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”. It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5 billion. nigeria.description: A 67-year-old blind Nigerian woman who has lived in the United Kingdom for 26 years has been told she may have to wait another 20 years before qualifying for permanent residency under proposed changes to the country’s immigration settlement rules. The woman, identified as Comfort, arrived in the UK in 2000 but lost her sight shortly afterwards after developing acute glaucoma. After spending 20 years in the country, she was granted permission to remain in 2022 under the long-residence immigration route. Under the arrangement, migrants are required to renew their visas every 30 months for 10 years before becoming eligible to apply for indefinite leave to remain, which allows them to live permanently in the UK. However, following new settlement rules announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, Comfort is likely to face an additional 20-year wait before qualifying for permanent residency, meaning she could be in her 80s by the time she becomes eligible. Concerned about her age and disability, lawyers at Refugee and Migrant Justice applied to the Home Office for her to be granted indefinite leave to remain immediately under provisions that allow exceptional cases to be fast-tracked. The application was rejected, with the Home Office initially telling her that she could return to Nigeria because services for blind people were available there. However, the refusal letter concluded: “Your circumstances are not so severe or lacking in potential treatment in India that it would warrant indefinite leave to remain in this case.” Comfort expressed disappointment over the decision, saying she had established her life in the UK and had no connection with India. “In 2022, I got my permission to stay here based on long residence in the UK,” she said. “I’m very disheartened that I may now need to wait nearly 20 years to get indefinite leave to remain. “I have been living in this country for 26 years. I have found my home here and settled well. I have my friends, my church and do voluntary work. nigeria.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
nigeria.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. entertainment.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. The question is how women-led enterprises can scale, command capital, influence policy and build institutions that endure. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. sports.title: 'Everyone knew': Ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers fires fresh salvo at Pat Cummins over sandpaper scandal
sports.description: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the South Africa tour. Sayers, who was part of the touring squad, said he believed every player was aware of what was happening. He also disagreed with Cummins’ statement that there was no team discussion about taking collective responsibility after the incident. “I’m comfortable sitting here … that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” Sayers told SEN radio on Sunday. “I’m not taking sides. I’m neutral in all this, I’m just trying to tell my side of the story and what I believe happened.” The controversy has returned to the spotlight following Khawaja’s autobiography, in which he claimed the entire team knew about the sandpaper plan and suggested Australia had used ball-tampering methods even before the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s allegations as “complete nonsense” during a press conference on Friday. However, Sayers was unhappy with how the Australian captain addressed the issue, particularly his personal comments about Khawaja. “I didn’t like how he [Cummins] did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I don’t think it needed to happen.” Sayers recalls team meeting after scandal Sayers also remembered a lengthy discussion among players after the incident came to light. This contradicts Cummins’ version of events. “We all sat in the change rooms after that day’s play, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, and just talked about what had happened and where to next,” Sayers said. He added that he was relieved the matter was finally being discussed openly after years of players having to remain silent. Warner questions Cricket Australia's investigation Meanwhile, former vice-captain David Warner has again questioned Cricket Australia’s investigation, alleging that important information was withheld from him. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was punished following the scandal. Warner claimed he was never informed that bowlers had been interviewed during the investigation and questioned why the governing body had not shared all the evidence with him before he accepted his punishment. “Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote on Instagram. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements. “That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. Why weren’t we given all the evidence by CA?”

sports.description: Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy in action at the DP World Tour Championship golf tournament at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai (Fadel SENNA) Rory McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai title to tie the record of Scotland's Colin Montgomerie after a dramatic final round of the season-ending $10 million DP World Tour Championship on Sunday. The tournament itself was a runaway win for England's Tyrrell Hatton (66) but all eyes were on the fascinating battle between McIlroy and Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, playing a group behind. It all came down to the 18th hole, where McIlroy made a disappointing par to finish on 10-under par, but that was good enough for a solo second place. That took his ranking points to 5,044.86. Chacarra also could not get a birdie on the final hole and closed with a 69 for a tied third place at eight-under alongside Finland's Oliver Lindell (65). The European number one crown was secured with a bogey-free round of five-under par 67, but it all came down to the par-4 16th hole, where he hit a magnificent second shot to a foot for the decisive birdie. McIlroy started with a birdie, but the momentum seemed to have been halted over the next four holes, when he burnt the edge on three but could not get a second birdie. He then picked up three shots over the next four holes, but Chacarra kept him in sight with four birdies in his first eight holes. When McIlroy could not make a birdie on the par-5 14th hole, Chacarra was leading the projected ranking by a mere 0.1 point. Hatton finally finished with seven birdies against a solitary mistake on the third hole on a day when he again dazzled with brilliant short iron and wedge play. The win was worth $3 million and he also climbed to third in the Race to Dubai behind McIlroy and Chacarra, his career best finish. sports.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown on Sunday after he finished in second place at the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy posted a superb final round score of 67 to finish two strokes clear of his main rival for the season-long race, Eugenio Chacarra. The Northern Irishman’s second-place finish at the Earth Course secured his fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title. Rory McIlroy has now tied Colin Montgomerie with eight Race to Dubai crowns. It’s fair to say that the six-time major champion was nowhere near his best this week in Dubai, but he did enough to get the job done in the end. Getting that eighth order of merit title under his belt was so important for McIlroy, and now his attention will turn to breaking the record next year. Chacarra came so close to winning his first season-long race, and he gave a great account of himself throughout 2026. Eugenio Chacarra’s reaction after Rory McIlroy wins the Race to Dubai The race between McIlroy and Chacarra went right down to the wire , and the Spaniard deserves huge credit for pushing the Northern Irishman all the way. After his final round on Sunday, Chacarra was asked to share his feelings after just missing out on the order of merit title. “ Yeah, it was a good fight. I just came up short, “ he admitted. “ That’s the beauty of golf, Obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And he’s played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. “ Yeah, I played good. I fought hard. I knew it was going to be a long day and I tried my best. That’s all I can ask for myself to do and that’s what we did. “ As I said yesterday, it was a bonus, and I would say proud of the fight and proud to have a chance till the end. “ Chacarra then commented on the prospect of playing on the PGA Tour next year. “ Yeah, super excited. sports.title: Dominant Australia defeat New Zealand in Men's World Cup final
sports.description: Australia have now won 23 consecutive World Cup matches since 2008 [Getty Images] Australia (24) 32 Tries: Martin 2, Bostock 2, Best, Trbojevic Goals: Munster 4 New Zealand (6) 12 Tries: McLean, Papali'i Goals: Isaako 2 Same old story. Having started the Rugby League World Cup in unconvincing fashion, Australia once again showed why they are masters of peaking for the big occasion as they defeated New Zealand 32-12 to be crowned champions for a fourth consecutive occasion. And this was never really close as the green and gold juggernaut pressed repeat on what has become a familiar pattern - and a depressing one for all those that have attempted to stop them since the Kiwis triumphed in Brisbane in the 2008 showpiece. Despite being outplayed and outmuscled by Stacey Jones' side in an epic opening to this tournament on 15 October, Australia still edged to a 24-22 victory. And five weeks on from that pulsating contest - perhaps stung by some observers questioning their credentials - Kevin Walters' team delivered conclusive proof that they remain the remain the benchmark for all others to aspire to. They were simply untouchable in the first-half, with a demonstration of power and quality that carried them into a 24-6 advantage at the break and a long way towards victory - their 23rd successive win in World Cup matches since that loss 18 years ago. Back on the ground where New Zealand delivered one of the most seismic shocks the international game has ever seen, there was never a moment where history threatened to repeat itself in front of a sell-out 52,500 crowd. Jones' team admittedly played a part in their own downfall. Jamayne Isaako's error from the kick-off set the tone and Australia ruthlessly punished it with Liam Martin bundling over to score from their first attack with just 84 seconds on the clock. While a converted try from the youngest player on the pitch, Casey McLean, briefly brought New Zealand level it was all they had to show from a disappointing first 40 minutes, when they repeatedly gifted Australia possession and field position. sports.title: Rory McIlroy wins Race to Dubai title for record-equalling eighth time
sports.description: Rory McIlroy has won the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, pipping Eugenio Chacarra to the crown. Spaniard Chacarra had held a slender 533.93-point lead over Masters champion McIlroy going into the season finale at Jumeirah Golf Estates. McIlroy, though, overturned that deficit after a blemish-free fourth round of 67 saw him finish on 10 under par, on his own in second, to take a fifth successive European tour crown, matching Colin Montgomerie ’s record of eight Order of Merit titles. Ryder Cup team-mate Tyrell Hatton , meanwhile, stormed to victory in Dubai, ending the day five shots ahead of second-placed McIlroy to round off a fantastic week. "Winning eight Order of Merits (now called Race to Dubai) was never in my list of goals growing up,” McIlroy said. "I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me. "I'm proud to be European and part of this tour." Visibly choked up, McIlroy revealed that his dad Gerry has been in hospital since undergoing "a huge operation in September" and said his triumph was for him. Rory McIlroy won the Race to Dubai title as Tyrell Hatton triumphed at the DP World Championship (Getty) He also reflected on the drama of the day and insisted he wasn’t aware of how “back and forth” the title fight with Chacarra was until he reached the 16th. "When I walked to the 16th green I saw Eugenio [Chacarra] was projected one, and when I walked off after my birdie I was projected one,” he added. "Eugenio played pretty good, but none of the chasing pack made a move and thankfully everything fell my way. "I pride myself in my consistency. I finished third last week, second this week. I feel like I've done a good job in recent years of not playing my way out of tournaments like I did earlier in my career." It was heartbreak for Chacarra, who needed to win the tournament to make sure he fended off McIlroy, as well as potentially several other big hitters in the chasing pack. Eugenio Chacarra was pipped to the crown (Getty) However, a final round of 69, which featured six birdies but also three bogeys either side of the turn, saw him come up just short at eight under in a tie for third, with other scores in the final groups also going McIlroy’s way. "It was a good fight. I just came out short. That's the beauty of golf,” he said. "Obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And McIlroy's played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. "I played good. I fought. I knew it was going to be a long day, and I tried my best. That's all I can ask for myself to do and that's what we did."

technology.title: LEO gets a birthday bash, 75 years after clocking in
technology.description: Business computing turns 75 this month, and Cambridge's Centre for Computing History is throwing a party for LEO, the machine that helped start it all. The LEO@75 event takes place on Saturday, November 28, from 10am to 5pm, with film screenings, historical displays, and hands-on activities for children. The Register has written about the Centre for Computing History a few times. It's an interactive computer museum just off Coldhams Lane in Cambridge, and back in 2018 it won National Lottery funding to help it "preserve, archive and digitise a range of LEO Computers artefacts, documents and personal memories." Admission supports the museum charity, with student and concession tickets at £10 and family tickets starting at £15. As well as stuff for the grown-ups, including a film screening, it will include events for smaller children (5-7) and a Python coding event for older (12-16) kids. Regular readers might recall our story about the Lyons Electronic Office back in 2021, celebrating its 70th anniversary. The Reg also published an obituary for Mary Coombs, the first female commercial programmer the following year. Coombs started programming LEO in 1952. Both stories offer more on the machine and the people behind it. LEO was an early computer, but from three-quarters of a century away, it's easy to miss just how early. Its design was based on Cambridge University's EDSAC, developed by a team led by the late, great Sir Maurice Wilkes. The Reg mentioned EDSAC in our obituary for Wilkes, and went into more detail for his centenary in 2013 . It also crops up in our Geek's Guide to Cambridge . The design of EDSAC was directly inspired by John von Neumann's famous, and incomplete, "First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC" – which The Reg talked about in 2011 . The draft report was circulated in 1945, based on the proposal for EDVAC, four years before the hardware was delivered. That was also the year John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert completed its predecessor, ENIAC. In its original form, ENIAC was programmed by setting switches and reconnecting cables; EDVAC, by contrast, was designed to store its instructions in memory. The report set out what's now called the "von Neumann architecture." Wilkes and Douglas Hartree drew on those ideas in developing EDSAC, LEO's immediate forerunner and one of the world's earliest practical stored-program computers. The first working electronic stored-program machine was the Manchester "Baby," the Small-Scale Experimental Machine, which ran its first program in 1948 . EDSAC ran its first program in May 1949 – a few months before the delivery of BINAC, Eckert and Mauchly's first stored-program machine. LEO ran its first commercial application in 1951. That was also the year the US Census Bureau took delivery of Eckert and Mauchly's UNIVAC I . ®

science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment."
